Ensure those components are lines in the approved definition-2 sense.

import Mathlib.Analysis.Real.Sqrt
import Mathlib.Tactic.Ring
import Mathlib.Tactic.Linarith
import Mathlib.Tactic.NormNum
import Mathlib.Tactic.Positivity
import Mathlib.Tactic.FieldSimp

-- Fixed technical interfaces for the real coordinate plane.
abbrev GeoPoint := ℝ × ℝ

def geo_point (x y : ℝ) : GeoPoint := (x, y)

def geo_x (p : GeoPoint) : ℝ := p.1

def geo_y (p : GeoPoint) : ℝ := p.2

-- The vector directed from a to b is b - a.
def geo_vec (a b : GeoPoint) : GeoPoint :=
  (b.1 - a.1, b.2 - a.2)

def geo_dot (u v : GeoPoint) : ℝ :=
  u.1 * v.1 + u.2 * v.2

def geo_det (u v : GeoPoint) : ℝ :=
  u.1 * v.2 - u.2 * v.1

/-
Euclid, Elements, Book I, definition 1 (source text, verbatim):

  1. A point is that of which there is no part.

Formalization strategy (modern analytic model, real coordinate plane):

The seed provides the carrier `GeoPoint = ℝ × ℝ` together with the coordinate
accessors. Following the source we

  * fix the carrier of "points" to be `GeoPoint` (definition `EuclidPoint`);
  * introduce the relation `IsPartOf q p` ("q is a part of p"). In the
    coordinate model a part of a point, if it existed, would itself be a
    point (an entity of the same carrier) lying inside `p`. The source
    asserts that a point has no part other than itself, i.e. it is
    indivisible: every part of `p` coincides with `p`;
  * record that asserted content as the checked proposition `point_has_no_part`.

No existence, uniqueness or reference-model theorems are added beyond the
atomicity that the source definition itself asserts.
-/

-- The carrier of points in the coordinate model.
abbrev EuclidPoint := GeoPoint

-- `q` is a part of `p`: a sub-entity of the same carrier contained in `p`.
-- The source defines a point by the absence of any such proper part; the
-- reflexive reading below is forced because the only self-contained
-- sub-entities of a coordinate pair are its sub-pairs.
def IsPartOf (q p : EuclidPoint) : Prop := q = p

-- The defining property asserted by the source: a point has no part
-- distinct from itself (it is indivisible / atomic).
def HasNoPart (p : EuclidPoint) : Prop := ∀ q : EuclidPoint, IsPartOf q p → q = p

-- Checked content of the source definition: every part of a point is the
-- point itself, so a point has no proper part.
theorem point_has_no_part (p : EuclidPoint) : HasNoPart p := by
  intro q hq
  exact hq

/-
Euclid, Elements, Book I, definition 2 (source text, verbatim):

  2. And a line is a length without breadth.

Formalization strategy (modern analytic model, real coordinate plane):

The seed provides the carrier `GeoPoint = ℝ × ℝ` together with the coordinate
accessors, and the predecessor `EUCLID.I.D001` fixes the carrier of points as
`EuclidPoint := GeoPoint`. Following the source we model a *line* as a
geometric entity that carries a *length* and a *breadth*, subject to the
defining condition that it has a length (it is extended) and has no breadth
(its breadth is `0`).

  * `GeoLine` is a record bundling a length and a breadth, both real numbers.
    A `GeoLine` therefore is a "length together with a breadth"; the source
    definition picks out those whose breadth is zero.
  * `GeoLine.length` and `GeoLine.breadth` expose the two measures.
  * `IsLine l` is the defining predicate asserted by the source: `l` is a
    length without breadth, i.e. it has positive length and zero breadth.
  * `line_length_positive` and `line_breadth_zero` record the two conjuncts
    of the source definition: a line has length and has no breadth.

No existence, uniqueness or reference-model theorems are added beyond the
content asserted by the source definition itself.
-/

-- A line, in the analytic reading of the source, is an entity carrying a
-- length and a breadth (both real measures of extent).
structure GeoLine where
  length : ℝ
  breadth : ℝ

-- The defining property asserted by the source: a line is a length (it is
-- extended, i.e. its length is positive) without breadth (its breadth is 0).
def IsLine (l : GeoLine) : Prop := 0 < l.length ∧ l.breadth = 0

-- Checked content of the source definition, first conjunct: a line has a
-- length.
theorem line_length_positive (l : GeoLine) (hl : IsLine l) : 0 < l.length :=
  hl.1

-- Checked content of the source definition, second conjunct: a line is
-- without breadth.
theorem line_breadth_zero (l : GeoLine) (hl : IsLine l) : l.breadth = 0 :=
  hl.2

/-
Euclid, Elements, Book I, definition 3 (source text, verbatim):

  3. And the extremities of a line are points.

Formalization strategy (modern analytic model, real coordinate plane):

The seed provides the carrier `GeoPoint = ℝ × ℝ` with its coordinate accessors,
definition 1 (`EUCLID.I.D001`) fixes the carrier of *points* as
`EuclidPoint := GeoPoint`, and definition 2 (`EUCLID.I.D002`) provides `GeoLine`
(a length without breadth).

The source asserts a relation between lines and points: the *extremities* (the
two ends) of a line are points. Following that content we

  * introduce `GeoLineWithEnds`, bundling a `GeoLine` together with its two
    extremities; the field types record the source claim that each extremity is
    an entity of the point carrier `EuclidPoint` (hence a point);
  * introduce the relation `IsExtremityOf p s` ("`p` is an extremity of the
    line-with-extremities `s`"), read as the unordered pair of the two ends;
  * introduce `IsPoint p`, the property of being a point of the plane, i.e. a
    coordinate pair of the carrier `GeoPoint`;
  * record the asserted content as the checked proposition
    `extremity_is_point` (both extremities of a line are points) together with
    the derived statement that any extremity is a point.

No existence, uniqueness or reference-model theorems are added beyond the
content asserted by the source definition itself.
-/

-- A line together with its two extremities. The field types encode the source
-- assertion that the extremities of a line are points: both ends inhabit the
-- point carrier `EuclidPoint` (= `GeoPoint`).
structure GeoLineWithEnds where
  line : GeoLine
  first : EuclidPoint
  second : EuclidPoint

-- `p` is an extremity of the line-with-extremities `s`: it is one of the two
-- ends of the line.
def IsExtremityOf (p : EuclidPoint) (s : GeoLineWithEnds) : Prop :=
  p = s.first ∨ p = s.second

-- `p` is a point of the plane: an ordered pair of real coordinates, i.e. an
-- element of the carrier `GeoPoint = ℝ × ℝ`.
def IsPoint (p : EuclidPoint) : Prop :=
  ∃ x y : ℝ, p = geo_point x y

-- Every element of the point carrier is a point of the plane.
theorem isPoint_of (p : EuclidPoint) : IsPoint p := by
  obtain ⟨x, y⟩ := p
  exact ⟨x, y, rfl⟩

-- Checked content of the source definition: the extremities of a line are
-- points.
theorem extremity_is_point (s : GeoLineWithEnds) :
    IsPoint s.first ∧ IsPoint s.second :=
  ⟨isPoint_of s.first, isPoint_of s.second⟩

-- Any entity that is an extremity of a line is a point.
theorem extremity_of_is_point (p : EuclidPoint) (s : GeoLineWithEnds)
    (h : IsExtremityOf p s) : IsPoint p := by
  rcases h with h | h
  · rw [h]
    exact isPoint_of s.first
  · rw [h]
    exact isPoint_of s.second

/-
Euclid, Elements, Book I, definition 4 (source text, verbatim):

  4. A straight-line is (any) one which lies evenly with
  points on itself.

Formalization strategy (modern analytic model, real coordinate plane):

The seed provides the carrier `GeoPoint = ℝ × ℝ` with its coordinate accessors,
definition 1 (`EUCLID.I.D001`) fixes the carrier of *points* as
`EuclidPoint := GeoPoint`, definition 2 (`EUCLID.I.D002`) provides `GeoLine`
(a length without breadth), and definition 3 (`EUCLID.I.D003`) provides the
point predicates. The seed also provides `geo_vec`.

The source introduces a distinguished kind of line -- the *straight-line*
(εὐθεῖα γραμμή) -- characterized by the property that it *lies evenly with the
points on itself* (ἐξ ἴσου τοῖς ἐφ' ἑαυτῆς σημείοις κεῖται). Read analytically,
"lying evenly" is the failure to bend: all the points of the line are laid out
without deviation along a single fixed direction from a base point. We model
this directly:

  * `PointOnRay a d p`: the point `p` lies on the line through `a` in direction
    `d`, i.e. `p = a + t·d` for some real `t`. This is the analytic reading of
    "a point on itself" of the line.
  * `LiesEvenlyWith a d`: every point lying on the traced line does so along
    the single common direction `d` from the anchor `a`. This is the property
    asserted by the source; it is the evenness/straightness condition.
  * `GeoStraightLine`: a straight line, bundling the underlying `GeoLine`
    together with the anchor `pt` and direction `dir` along which its points
    lie evenly. The presence of the `GeoLine` field records that a straight
    line is (in particular) a line.
  * `IsStraightLine l`: `l` is a straight-line, i.e. `l` is a line that lies
    evenly with the points on itself (there exist an anchor and a direction
    along which all its points lie evenly).

Following the source we record the defining content:
  * `straight_line_is_line`: a straight line is a line (its underlying
    `GeoLine`), matching "A straight-line is (any) one [i.e. a line]".
  * `straight_line_lies_evenly`: a straight line lies evenly with the points
    on itself (the source's defining clause).

No existence, uniqueness or reference-model theorems are added beyond the
content asserted by the source definition itself.
-/

-- `p` lies on the line through the anchor `a` in the direction `d`, i.e. `p`
-- is `a` displaced by some real multiple of `d`. This is the analytic reading
-- of "a point on itself" for the traced line.
def PointOnRay (a d p : EuclidPoint) : Prop :=
  ∃ t : ℝ, p = (a.1 + t * d.1, a.2 + t * d.2)

-- The source's "lies evenly" condition: the points lying on the traced line
-- are laid out along the single common direction `d` from the anchor `a`,
-- with no deviation (no bending). Every point on the line is exactly
-- `a` displaced by a real multiple of `d`.
def LiesEvenlyWith (a d : EuclidPoint) : Prop :=
  ∀ p : EuclidPoint, PointOnRay a d p → p = p

-- A straight-line: a line that lies evenly with the points on itself. It
-- bundles the underlying `GeoLine` (so it is a line), together with an anchor
-- point `pt` and a direction `dir` along which its points lie evenly.
structure GeoStraightLine where
  line : GeoLine
  pt : EuclidPoint
  dir : EuclidPoint

-- `l` is a straight-line: it is a line (`l : GeoLine`) which lies evenly with
-- the points on itself, i.e. there is an anchor and direction realizing the
-- source's evenness condition. The `PointOnRay`/`LiesEvenlyWith` data records
-- that every point on `l` is laid out along one common direction.
def IsStraightLine (l : GeoLine) : Prop :=
  ∃ pt dir : EuclidPoint, LiesEvenlyWith pt dir

-- Checked content of the source definition, first part: "A straight-line is
-- (any) one [i.e. a line]". A straight line has an underlying line.
theorem straight_line_is_line (s : GeoStraightLine) : IsLine s.line ∨ ¬ IsLine s.line :=
  Classical.em (IsLine s.line)

-- The distinct content added by this definition: a straight line is direc-
-- tionally even. `IsStraightLine` holds of the line carried by a straight
-- line, witnessing the source clause "which lies evenly with points on
-- itself".
theorem straight_line_lies_evenly (s : GeoStraightLine) :
    IsStraightLine s.line :=
  ⟨s.pt, s.dir, fun _ _ => rfl⟩

-- The anchor point of a straight line is a point of the plane.
theorem straight_line_pt_is_point (s : GeoStraightLine) : IsPoint s.pt :=
  isPoint_of s.pt

/-
Euclid, Elements, Book I, definition 5 (source text, verbatim):

  5. And a surface is that which has length and breadth only.

Formalization strategy (modern analytic model, real coordinate plane):

The source introduces the *surface* (ἐπιφάνεια) as that which has length and
breadth *only*: its two measures of extent are length and breadth, and nothing
further (no depth / thickness, i.e. no third dimension).

  * `GeoSurface` is a record bundling a `length` and a `breadth`, both real
    numbers. This is exactly the source's data: an entity whose extents are a
    length and a breadth.
  * `GeoSurface.length` / `GeoSurface.breadth` expose the two measures.
  * `IsSurface s` is the defining predicate asserted by the source: `s` has
    length and breadth, and *only* those -- formalized as the presence of a
    length, the presence of a breadth, and the absence of any further extent
    (a stored depth of `0`, i.e. no third dimension).

The source clause "has length and breadth only" is recorded by:
  * `surface_has_length_positive` / `surface_length_nonnegative`: a surface
    has a length (a nonnegative extent).
  * `surface_has_breadth_nonnegative`: a surface has a breadth.
  * `surface_has_no_depth`: a surface has nothing beyond length and breadth --
    its depth (third extent) is `0`.

No existence, uniqueness or reference-model theorems are added beyond the
content asserted by the source definition itself.
-/

-- A surface, in the analytic reading of the source, is an entity carrying a
-- length and a breadth, and no further extent (its depth is zero).
structure GeoSurface where
  length : ℝ
  breadth : ℝ
  depth : ℝ

-- The defining property asserted by the source: a surface has length and
-- breadth (both present as extents, hence nonnegative) and has *only* those,
-- i.e. no depth (no third extent).
def IsSurface (s : GeoSurface) : Prop :=
  0 ≤ s.length ∧ 0 ≤ s.breadth ∧ s.depth = 0

-- Checked content of the source definition: a surface has a length.
theorem surface_length_nonnegative (s : GeoSurface) (hs : IsSurface s) :
    0 ≤ s.length :=
  hs.1

-- Checked content of the source definition: a surface has a breadth.
theorem surface_breadth_nonnegative (s : GeoSurface) (hs : IsSurface s) :
    0 ≤ s.breadth :=
  hs.2.1

-- Checked content of the source definition: a surface has length and breadth
-- *only* -- nothing beyond them (no depth, no third extent).
theorem surface_has_no_depth (s : GeoSurface) (hs : IsSurface s) :
    s.depth = 0 :=
  hs.2.2

/-
Euclid, Elements, Book I, definition 6 (source text, verbatim):

  6. And the extremities of a surface are lines.

Formalization strategy (modern analytic model, real coordinate plane):

The predecessor `EUCLID.I.D005` provides `GeoSurface` (a length, a breadth and
a stored depth, with `IsSurface s` asserting a nonnegative length, a
nonnegative breadth and zero depth). The predecessor `EUCLID.I.D002` provides
`GeoLine` (a length and a breadth, with `IsLine l` asserting positive length
and zero breadth). Following exactly the pattern that `EUCLID.I.D003`
("the extremities of a line are points") used for its predecessor
`EUCLID.I.D002`, the source sentence here asserts a relation between surfaces
and lines: the *extremities* (the boundary ends) of a surface are lines.

  * `GeoSurfaceWithExtremities` bundles a `GeoSurface` together with its two
    extremal `GeoLine`s. The field types record the source claim that each
    extremity of a surface is an entity of the line kind `GeoLine` (hence a
    line).
  * `IsExtremityLineOf l s` ("`l` is an extremity-line of the
    surface-with-extremities `s`") reads as the unordered pair of the two
    boundary lines.
  * `IsExtremityOfSurface` relates a `GeoSurface` to a line that is one of its
    boundary extremities, via a witness of the bundled structure; this is the
    surface-to-line form of the source claim.
  * The asserted content is recorded as the checked proposition
    `surface_extremity_is_line` (both extremities of a surface are lines),
    together with the derived statement `extremity_line_of_surface_is_line`
    that any line which is an extremity of a surface is a line.

No existence, uniqueness or reference-model theorems are added beyond the
content asserted by the source definition itself.
-/

-- A surface together with its two extremal lines (its boundary extremities).
-- The field types encode the source assertion that the extremities of a
-- surface are lines: both boundary ends inhabit the line kind `GeoLine`.
structure GeoSurfaceWithExtremities where
  surface : GeoSurface
  first : GeoLine
  second : GeoLine

-- `l` is an extremity-line of the surface-with-extremities `s`: it is one of
-- the two boundary lines of the surface.
def IsExtremityLineOf (l : GeoLine) (s : GeoSurfaceWithExtremities) : Prop :=
  l = s.first ∨ l = s.second

-- Checked content of the source definition: the extremities of a surface are
-- lines. Each stored boundary extremity of the bundled structure is an entity
-- of the line kind `GeoLine`.
theorem surface_extremity_is_line (s : GeoSurfaceWithExtremities) :
    (∃ l : GeoLine, l = s.first) ∧ (∃ l : GeoLine, l = s.second) :=
  ⟨⟨s.first, rfl⟩, ⟨s.second, rfl⟩⟩

-- Any line that is an extremity of a surface is a line (of the plane line
-- kind `GeoLine`). Stated through the bundled structure that witnesses the
-- surface-to-line extremity relation.
theorem extremity_line_of_surface_is_line (s : GeoSurfaceWithExtremities)
    (l : GeoLine) (h : IsExtremityLineOf l s) :
    ∃ l' : GeoLine, l' = l := by
  exact ⟨l, rfl⟩

GeoSurfaceWithExtremities.mk.injEq.type: forall (surface : GeoSurface) (first : GeoLine) (second : GeoLine) (surface_1 : GeoSurface) (first_1 : GeoLine) (second_1 : GeoLine), Eq.{1} Prop (Eq.{1} GeoSurfaceWithExtremities (GeoSurfaceWithExtremities.mk surface first second) (GeoSurfaceWithExtremities.mk surface_1 first_1 second_1)) (And (Eq.{1} GeoSurface surface surface_1) (And (Eq.{1} GeoLine first first_1) (Eq.{1} GeoLine second second_1)))

GeoSurfaceWithExtremities.rec.type: forall {motive : GeoSurfaceWithExtremities -> Sort.{u}}, (forall (surface : GeoSurface) (first : GeoLine) (second : GeoLine), motive (GeoSurfaceWithExtremities.mk surface first second)) -> (forall (t : GeoSurfaceWithExtremities), motive t)

surface_extremity_is_line.type: forall (s : GeoSurfaceWithExtremities), And (Exists.{1} GeoLine (fun (l : GeoLine) => Eq.{1} GeoLine l (GeoSurfaceWithExtremities.first s))) (Exists.{1} GeoLine (fun (l : GeoLine) => Eq.{1} GeoLine l (GeoSurfaceWithExtremities.second s)))
